question.problem:
Given the function  $y=4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}+5$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}+5) \\  & =\frac{4}{x}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(\frac{4}{x}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2))|}_{x=2} \\  & =\frac{4}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\  & =2-\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,.\end{aligned}
$$
